threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You can spot the newcomers by their bewildered looks when the Tube strikes hit—like, haven’t they heard this is our second home now?
Last night on the 196, a couple was arguing about whether or not they could fit their takeaway in the overhead rack. It was a tight squeeze, but they made it work.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: Walking past the Turkish market on Monday, I spotted a guy haggling over the price of baklava while a hipster juggled coffee cups. Classic Neukölln moment.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Berlin can you find a hidden club in a former factory basement, complete with a dance floor that used to be a giant swimming pool.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You can spot a local by their reaction to BART delays—rolling their eyes like it’s an old friend. Tourists just look lost and frustrated.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Saw a guy in a tuxedo getting off the 38 Geary, holding a bouquet. Guessing he was late to the wedding, but Muni never cares about your plans.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think Gràcia is all about Gaudí, but the real charm is in the small plazas where locals sip their café, far from the hustle.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can tell by the bewildered looks when they order a 'café con leche' and expect a small cup, not a full glass.

threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still think the bus timetable is a suggestion, not a cruel joke. You’ll learn the route by heart soon enough.
Last night on the N35, a guy tried to sell a rubber chicken like it was street art. The driver just shook his head and kept driving. Classic Brixton.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: I knew I was home when I stumbled into a hidden yard sale on a Sunday morning, haggling over vintage records while kids played by with old roller skates.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Kreuzberg can you sip a beer while watching an impromptu breakdance battle at a bus stop – it's like performance art meets public transport.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You know someone’s local when they know to avoid the 14 Mission after 5 PM; it’s like riding a rollercoaster of delays and cranky commuters.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Saw a guy playing a saxophone in the back of a crowded bus—he started a spontaneous sing-along. Only in the Mission, right?

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think all the bars in Gràcia close early, but the hidden corners open up after midnight, full of locals and unlit ambiance.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can spot a recent arrival in Gràcia by their tendency to order 'café con leche' and then stare blankly when the barista only responds in Catalan.
